stepAnswer: $$v_1$$ and $$v_4$$ because the columns of $$V$$ must be orthonormal
stepBody:
Justin would like to perform PCA analysis on the $$	ext{ed\_replies}$$ dataset. He asks Hannah to provide him the necessary data. She first subsets the DataFrame to only the features using the following code:
$$	exttt{ed\_subset}$$ $$=$$ $$	exttt{ed\_replies[['length',}$$ $$	exttt{'likes','response\_time']]}$$
Then, Hannah randomly samples a number of rows of $$	ext{ed\_subset}$$ and converts the resulting DataFrame into a matrix denoted by $$X$$
Hannah performs SVD on $$X$$
Recall that in SVD, $$X$$ is decomposed into the product of $$3$$ matrices, denoted $$ \cup , S$$ and $$V**{T}$$ (using the same naming convention as lecture). Hannah only sends Justin the complete matrix $$S$$ (the singular values).
$$S$$ is a $$3$$ by $$3$$ diagonal matrix with diagonal entries $$(100, 88, 8)$$
Hannah sends four mystery vectors $$v_1$$ $$v_2$$ $$v_3$$ and $$v_4$$ to Justin, two of which are columns of $$V$$
She also sends over two tables containing information about the vectors. The first table reports the L2 norm of each vector:
• the norm of $$v_1$$ is $$1$$
• the norm of $$v_2$$ is $$1$$
• the norm of $$v_3$$ is $$2$$
• the norm of $$v_4$$ is $$1$$
The second table reports the pairwise dot product between the vectors:
• the dot product of $$v_1$$ and $$v_2$$ is $$1$$
• the dot product of $$v_1$$ and $$v_3$$ is $$0$$
• the dot product of $$v_1$$ and $$v_4$$ is $$0$$
• the dot product of $$v_2$$ and $$v_3$$ is $$0$$
• the dot product of $$v_2$$ and $$v_4$$ is $$8$$
• the dot product of $$v_3$$ and $$v_4$$ is $$100$$
Identify which two of the four vectors are the columns of $$V$$ along with the correct justification.
answerLatex: $$v_1$$ and $$v_4$$ because the columns of $$V$$ must be orthonormal
choices: $$v_1$$ and $$v_2$$ because they both have norm $$1$$
$$v_2$$ and $$v_3$$ because their dot product is $$0$$
$$v_1$$ and $$v_4$$ because the columns of $$V$$ must be orthonormal
$$v_3$$ and $$v_4$$ because their dot product equals the largest singular value
$$v_2$$ and $$v_4$$ because they have norm $$1$$ and a nonzero dot product
